reader.title: Attempted lynching of Charles Huff
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: A mob captured Charles Huff, accused as a cattle thief, and hanged him to a tree, but police intervened and he was cut down alive (A1, A4, A5).

A mob, many of whose members were reported wounded, hanged Huff as a cattle thief without legal authority, but he was cut down and resuscitated, so no one was killed; this was an attempted lynching (A1, A4, A5).
The three accounts of the hanging (A1, A4, A5) are versions of one Denver wire dispatch; a separate Denver dispatch (A2) reports a cattle-theft trial of a Huff but does not mention the mob.

summary.text: The attempted lynching of Charles Huff took place on the morning of July 12, 1882, when a mob captured Huff, described as a young cattle thief, and hanged him to a tree five miles from Denver, Colorado.
Police attacked the mob, and Huff was cut down and resuscitated.
None of the reports give Huff's race.

A separate Denver dispatch of the same date reported that 'Deutch-niatf' and Huff, called "two notorious cattle thieves," were on trial in police court for shooting calves and selling the carcasses to Denver dealers.
According to that dispatch, both were held in $750 each for the district court, but it does not mention a mob, and the coverage does not show whether the two dispatches concern the same man.
According to the Denver wire report, the mob seized Huff that morning and hanged him to a tree outside the city.
A squad of police then attacked the mob, and a "desperate fight" with gunfire followed.
While the fight was in progress, Huff was cut down and resuscitated, and the mob was routed.
No report of arrests of mob members, an inquiry, or the outcome of Huff's district-court case appears in the coverage.
The story circulated as a short wire item, which the New Haven Morning Journal and Courier ran on July 13 under the headline "A Young Cattle Thief's Peril."
The Middlebury Register in Vermont and the Daily Kennebec Journal in Maine reprinted it among miscellaneous general notes on July 14 and 15.
Every version called Huff a cattle thief without qualification and made no comment on the mob or the police.
The wire versions differed on the injuries: two said many of the mob were wounded, while the Middlebury Register said a number of participants were "sightly wounded."
